title: Roguelike Level Design: Random Pool Architecture and Build Power Scaling
subtitle: A deep dive into constructing random pools and managing build power curves in Roguelikes. This guide details room event pool configuration, weight constraints, and budget-based allocation strategies to prevent power creep. It covers techniques for ensuring key node appearances, implementing soft-correction mechanics for player progression, and designing explainable randomness to deliver a rich yet balanced procedural generation system.

breakdown.title: Building the Random Pool
bullets: Decompose levels into 'Room Template Pools': Standard, Elite, Shop, Event, Supply, etc.
Attach tags and constraints to each template: biome, difficulty tier, prerequisites/mutual exclusivity, cooldowns (to prevent consecutive spawns)
Use 'Budgets' instead of pure weights: Define target ratios for events and combat per layer or segment

breakdown.title: Controlling Build Power
bullets: Define target power curves: Expected growth in DPS/survival/mobility per layer
Reward distribution driven by tables: Ratios of upgrades/rarity/resources vary by layer
Implement 'Soft Correction': Compensate for falling behind, increase risk for leading instead of direct nerfs

breakdown.title: Avoiding 'Seemingly Random' Experiences
bullets: Prevent consecutive same-type rooms: Apply cooldowns to recent N category entries
Guarantee appearance at key nodes: e.g., at least one Shop/Supply every 3 layers
Make random results explainable: Use UI to inform players if the current layer is 'Combat-heavy' or 'Resource-heavy'
